headline: Building in Brooklyn falls into a construction site

sources.title: Brooklyn building collapse live updates: Dangerous search for survivors continues in NYC (CNN)
At least 2 killed, 17 hurt in Brooklyn building collapse, officials say (CBS New York)
Brooklyn building collapse kills at least two people and traps others in wreckage (The Guardian)
Flatbush collapse investigation focuses on building's history, nearby construction (ABC7 New York)

chunks.text: On November 11, 2026, a three-story building in Brooklyn, part of New York City, {{came down}} just after 4 p.m. It had a store on the [[ground floor]] and apartments above. Its walls {{caved in}}, and it fell into a [[construction site]] next door. At least two people died and at least 17 were [[injured]], fire officials said that night. Four were in [[critical condition]], so their lives were in danger. Seven children were among those [[treated]].

verbs.why: Many old trees come down in big storms. Old walls often come down in an earthquake. A three-story building in Brooklyn came down on the afternoon of November 11, 2026.
Old roofs sometimes cave in under heavy snow. The sides of a deep hole can cave in after rain. The building's walls caved in, and it fell into a construction site next door.

chunks.text: The building was built in 1930. Next to it, a one-story building had been {{knocked down}} for a new [[building project]]. Workers there were digging into the ground when the building fell, the fire department's top chief said. The city's Department of Buildings is trying to {{figure out}} the cause. It is not yet clear whether the work next door [[played a part]]. [[Inspectors]] are checking nearby buildings to make sure they are safe.

verbs.why: The city knocks down empty buildings that are not safe. Some owners knock down old houses and build bigger ones. Next to the Brooklyn building, a one-story building had been knocked down for a new building project.
Mechanics figure out what is wrong with a car. Doctors figure out the cause of a fever with a few tests. The city's Department of Buildings is trying to figure out the cause of the collapse.

chunks.text: More than 250 firefighters and [[emergency medical workers]] came to help. The first fire trucks {{pulled up}} about one minute after the first call. Crews {{carried out}} a careful, dangerous search. They moved the [[rubble]], the broken pieces of the building, mostly [[by hand]]. [[Rescue dogs]] helped them. Some firefighters {{broke through}} a fallen wall to search under it. Early that evening, they {{dug out}} a [[pregnant]] woman. Her husband told reporters she was alive.

verbs.correct: To drive to a place and stop
verbs.why: The school bus pulls up at the corner every morning. An ambulance pulls up in front of the house. The first fire trucks pulled up about one minute after the first call for help.

verbs.correct: To do a job or task
verbs.wrong: To pay for a job or task
verbs.why: Doctors carry out tests to check your blood. Firefighters carry out training every week. In Brooklyn, crews carried out a careful, dangerous search of the rubble.

verbs.correct: To force a way past something
verbs.why: Firefighters often break through a locked door to reach people inside. Rescuers sometimes break through thick ice to save a dog. Some firefighters in Brooklyn broke through a fallen wall to search under it.

verbs.correct: To free someone who is trapped
verbs.why: After an earthquake, rescuers dig out people from fallen homes. Ski patrol teams dig out skiers who are stuck under snow. Early that evening, firefighters dug out a pregnant woman from the rubble.

chunks.text: Part of the [[side wall]] of a second building was {{torn off}}, so people could see into its apartments. At least eight families had to leave their homes. The Red Cross and the city opened a [[help center]] for them. Officials do not yet know how many people may be [[missing]]. New York City's mayor praised the rescuers for their [[quick response]]. Fire officials said crews would {{keep up}} the search for several days.

verbs.why: Strong winds sometimes tear off the roofs of houses. Big storms tear off branches from old trees. Part of the side wall of a second building in Brooklyn was torn off.
The workers keep up the repairs all through the night. Fans keep up the cheering until the end of the game. Fire officials said crews would keep up the search in Brooklyn for several days.

mainIdea.s: A building in Brooklyn fell into the construction site next to it, and at least two people died. Rescuers searched the rubble by hand, and officials are studying what caused it.
mainIdea.why: The building came down on November 11, 2026, and at least 17 people were hurt. The city is trying to figure out the cause, and crews will keep up the search.

mainIdea.s: An old apartment building in New York collapsed beside a work site and killed two people. City leaders have already blamed the digging there, and crews ended their search that night.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the cause is not known yet. The city is trying to figure it out, and fire officials said crews would keep up the search for several days.

mainIdea.s: Workers finished a tall new apartment tower in Brooklyn after five long years of building. Officials call it one of the safest homes in the city, and families may live there by spring.
mainIdea.why: This story is about a building that fell into a construction site. At least two people died, and crews carried out a careful search by hand.

tf.s: Firefighters dug out a pregnant woman from the rubble.

lines.text: Did you see the news from Brooklyn?
About the building? I saw a video. It just {{came down}}.
Yeah, on November 11. The walls {{caved in}}, and it fell into a construction site next door.
Yes. At least two people died, and at least 17 were hurt. Seven of the people treated were kids.
More than 250 firefighters and medical workers came. The first fire trucks {{pulled up}} in about a minute.
That's fast. In a rescue like that, [[every second counts]].
It was [[all hands on deck]]. They {{carried out}} the search mostly by hand, with buckets.
They {{dug out}} a pregnant woman. Her husband said she's alive.
Wow, she's [[a real fighter]]. I hope she's [[safe and sound]] now.
Me too. But nobody knows yet how many people are still missing.
[[That's the scary part]]. Do they know why it fell?
Not yet. The city is trying to {{figure it out}}. Workers were digging next door.
So the work next door caused it?
Nobody knows that yet. For now, crews will {{keep up}} the search for several days.

expressions.def: Used to say that acting fast is very important
ex: When someone has a heart attack, every second counts.

expressions.def: Used to say that everyone is helping because there is a lot to do
ex: The restaurant was full, so it was all hands on deck in the kitchen.

expressions.def: Someone who is strong and keeps trying in a very hard situation
ex: My grandma beat cancer twice. She's a real fighter.
The tiny puppy was very weak, but it lived. It's a real fighter.
The lost children were found safe and sound.
We got home safe and sound after the long drive.

expressions.def: Used to say which part of a situation worries you most
ex: The storm could hit at night. That's the scary part.
Nobody knows how the fire started. That's the scary part.
